title: Until prompt fix: "until" stays an order
eyebrow: prompt fix · generator and critic prompts · 2026-11-20
subtitle: At reasoning max the generator and the critic read "until the door has been opened once" as a ban for the whole episode, because one prompt example matched the event's description almost word for word. Rewording two existing passages, with no new rule, fixed it: the targeted runs went from 2 of 9 right to 12 of 12, and the full 46-case rerun got 46 of 46.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text:
The generator turns a task into Declare clauses, and the critic checks them. Two cards say "do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once" (G6 and W5b). The right reading is an order: no drop before the door's first opening, `Precedence(door_open, key_lost)`; once the door has been opened, a drop is allowed. Both models wrote `Absence(key_lost)` instead, a ban for the whole episode, in 6 of 6 runs.

The prompt said: when the banned event's own description already holds the condition, write a plain `Absence`, for example an event "described as 'lost before `a` happened'". The environment page describes `key_lost` as "no longer carrying it before opening the door". Those are almost the same words, so both models matched the example and dropped the order. The fix rewords that example and says that "until `a`" is always `Precedence(a, b)`.

A second, rarer miss was in W5a: "Then open the door with the key and pick up the box" became two goals with no order (1 of 3 runs). The fix adds the case of steps listed after a leading "then" to the existing stated-order text. No rule was added.

items: **Prompt side, not pipeline side.** Every wrong run was the critic accepting the generator's first answer (2 calls per run), and no call failed. The generator and critic prompts share the templates file `declare-templates.md`, so its example misled both.

**No new rule.** Five edits in two files reword existing text: the ban-with-a-condition point and the stated-order point in the generator prompt, plus the matching table rows and worked example in `declare-templates.md`. A "while ... still closed" condition the event already holds still folds into `Absence` (W5a, G5, W4b and U5 kept it). "Until `a`" is now always `Precedence(a, b)`.
**G2 stays unordered.** "Open the door and pick up the box in the other room." has no order word. After the "then" edit it still gives two goals with no `Precedence`, as before.

**Published practice.** Anthropic's prompting guide warns that models copy details from examples (cited under "The change"). The two models here are not Claude; the guide served as the published practice the retry rule asks for.

items: **Main's full run is older.** Main's last full 46-case run at max is the loop-2 thinking sweep (`../model-comparison/`, its `evidence/llm-loop2/runs/f-max/A/`). It ran before the shape-fix sentence of `42003cf` and before streaming. Re-scored with today's cards it gets 44 of 46, with G6 and W5b wrong in the same `Absence` reading. It is the closest full baseline, not a same-prompt control; the targeted before round is.
**The fix was tried once per mistake.** Each edit fixed its cases on its first try (12 of 12), so no change was undone. The model-call count was 164 over 82 runs, with no usage-limit error.

**What is not tested.** After the fix the critic accepted the generator's first answer every time, so the critic never judged a wrong set under the new wording. W5a is weak evidence: about 1 miss in 8 before (counting an earlier max sweep), 4 of 4 after.

sections.title: G6: "until" with a goal
sections.intro: Task: *Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.* (templates suite, card `tpl-precedence-2-goal`, MiniGrid-DoorKey-8x8-v0). The environment page: "`key_lost`: The agent previously acquired the yellow key but is no longer carrying it before opening the door."

blocks.title: What the critic said before the fix
blocks.text:
G6 r3: "key_lost is defined as the key being dropped while the door is not open, so its description already holds the 'while the door is closed / before the door has been opened' condition; the plain hard Absence(key_lost) is exactly the prescribed ban for 'do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once', and no Precedence(door_open, key_lost) is needed".

W5b r1: "The event key_lost is defined as acquiring the key and then dropping it while the door is not open ('no longer carrying it before opening the door'), so its description already holds the condition and a plain Absence is the right template".

**`g6-before`** · DoorKey-8x8 · 3 states, 3 transitions · final u2, rejecting u1
Task: *Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.* Wrong, 3 of 3 runs: Absence(key_lost) bans dropping the key for the whole episode; the card expects Precedence(door_open, key_lost), which allows it once the door has been opened. The critic accepted it each time.

sections.title: W5a: the dropped "then"
sections.intro: Task: *Move the ball away from the door before you take the key. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards. Then open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room.* (complex suite, card `cx-goal-many-rules`, MiniGrid-BlockedUnlockPickup-v0). Here "try not to drop the key while the door is still closed" is a soft `Absence(key_lost)`: a "while ... still closed" ban the event already holds, which the fix keeps.

rows: hard Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key): `(((~has_door_key)Ublocker_moved)|(G(~has_door_key)))`; soft Absence(key_lost): `(~(Fkey_lost))`; soft Response(has_door_key, door_open): `(G(has_door_key->(Fdoor_open)))`; hard Precedence(has_door_key, door_open): `(((~door_open)Uhas_door_key)|(G(~door_open)))`; hard Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up): `(((~target_picked_up)Udoor_open)|(G(~target_picked_up)))`; hard Existence(target_picked_up): `(Ftarget_picked_up)`

blocks.text: In the miss (before r3) the generator wrote the last sentence as "Open the door at least once." and "Pick up the mission's designated target box at least once.", and the critic read it as "hard Existence(door_open), hard Precedence(has_door_key, door_open), and hard Existence(target_picked_up)". The prompt's stated-order text showed only lists where "then" comes before the last step ("`a`, `b`, `c`, and then `d`"), not a list after a leading "then".

sections.title: The change
sections.intro: Commit `40e6614` rewords existing text in `app/src/prompts/compiler-rm/reward-ltlf-creator.system.md` (the generator) and `app/src/prompts/compiler-rm/declare-templates.md` (shared by the generator and the critic: `app/src/prompts/loaders.py` splits it into both system prompts). The critic's own file is unchanged. Full diff: `evidence/prompt-fix.diff`.

items: **The example that misled.** The ban-with-a-condition example was an event "described as 'lost before `a` happened'"; it is now an event "described as 'dropped while the gate is shut'", and only a "while ... still shut" condition folds into `Absence`.

**"Until" is always an order.** The point, the table row and the worked example now say that "until `a`" is always `Precedence(a, b)`, "even when `b` is 'dropped while the gate is shut'", because `b` can happen again after the gate opens and shuts, and the task allows it then.
**A list after a leading "then" keeps its order.** The stated-order point and the "listed sequence" row now also cover "then / finally / after that, do `c` and `d`": `c` before `d`.

blocks.text: **Generator prompt, the two edited points (from evidence/prompt-fix.diff)**

- A stated order of commanded steps ("`a`, then `b`, then `c`", "first `a`, then `b`", "do `a` before
-  `b`") is the `Existence` of the last step plus one `Precedence` per consecutive pair:
+  `b`", and the steps listed after a leading "then", "finally" or "after that": "then do `b` and
+  `c`" is `b` before `c`) is the `Existence` of the last step plus one `Precedence` per consecutive pair:

- A ban with a condition ("while ... is still shut", "until ..."): first read the banned
-  event's description in the environment. If it already holds that condition (an event
-  described as "lost before `a` happened"), write plain `Absence` of that event and no
-  `Precedence`. Otherwise
-  the condition stays in the clause as `Precedence` of the event that ends it.
+  event's description in the environment. If it already holds a "while ... is still shut"
+  condition (an event described as "dropped while the gate is shut"), write plain `Absence`
+  of that event and no `Precedence`. Otherwise, and always for "until `a`" ("until the gate
+  has been opened once"), the condition stays in the clause as `Precedence` of the event
+  that ends it: the ban ends once `a` has happened, even if the gate shuts again later.

**Practice cited.** Anthropic, *Prompting best practices*, section "Use examples effectively": make examples "Diverse: Cover edge cases and vary enough that Claude doesn't pick up unintended patterns" ([platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices), read 2026-11-20). Its earlier Claude 4 version has the section the coder cited, "Be vigilant with examples & details": models "pay close attention to details and examples", so examples should match the wanted behavior ([docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices)). The coder also cited "Use examples (multishot prompting)" for the "then" edit: an example list should include the case you want.

items: **Run records:** `evidence/runs/before-max/` (9), `fix-until/` (6), `fix-then/` (3), `regression-fail/` (3), `regression-pass/` (15), `full-after/` (46). Each run has `<case>-r<k>.json` (task, clauses, critic trail, machine, wall) and a slim call log `<case>-r<k>.calls.jsonl` (timing, tokens, errors; prompts and schema dropped by `tools/slim_calls.py`). Main's full run is read from `../model-comparison/evidence/llm-loop2/runs/f-max/A/` and not copied.
**Tables:** `evidence/round-table.out`, the round table above; `tools/run_table.py` prints the per-run rows.
**Machines:** `graphs/<name>.rm` is the `machine` field of the record named under each graph, drawn as `.svg` and `.html`.

**Scripts:** `tools/round_table.py`, `tools/run_table.py` and the scorer they import (`arm_stats.py`, `chain_score.py`, `cases.py`, `loopcrit.py`, the same as in `../opencode-streaming/tools/`). The local cards they read are in `evidence/cards/`; the benchmark cards come from the checkout named by `CC_ROOT`. The tools that call the models stay in the plan folder.
**Limits:** 3 runs per targeted case before and 4 after, plus one full rerun; the critic side of the fix is untested (see above).
